lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 70, which runs fewer CI jobs, edits fewer comments, and stops rebuilding after a merge.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request seventy, which runs fewer CI jobs, edits fewer comments, and stops rebuilding after a merge.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Release folded into build, the report job run only for a fix, unchanged comments left alone, and debs reused after a merge.
On a PR, the review job now writes its own comment, unless it has a fix to push.
When a comment's new text is the same as the old, CI skips the edit, so nobody is woken.
A screenshot audit comment now updates the summary directly, instead of re-running a job.
The PR still shows the same checks; the report job is simply skipped when there's no fix.
On a push to main, build looks for the merged PR's run whose build and verify passed.
It reuses that run's debs only when they were built from the same files, with the same version.
The release is now published at the end of the build job.
And when the debs were reused, verify doesn't run again.
Actions ran out of minutes on 7 November, partly because GitHub rounds every short job up to a whole minute.
lines.say: Actions ran out of minutes on the seventh of November, partly because GitHub rounds every short job up to a whole minute.

lines.caption: So folding a ten-second job into one that already runs saves a whole billed minute.
Most reviews leave no fix, so the review job posts its findings itself, without the push token.
A fix still goes to the separate report job, so the model never shares a machine with the token.
The comment script reads the comment first, and skips the edit when the new body is identical.
The summary workflow now runs the summary script itself, once the head's build run has finished.
The changes step, the no-code markers and ccache all stay, and the merge rule allows the skipped report job.
A new script finds the merged PR's newest run with verified debs, from a branch of this repo, not a fork.
PR builds now stamp the next release version and record their file tree, so the push can compare both.
The release steps run at the end of build on a push, so build may now write to the repo.
Reused debs skip verify, since the PR's run already tested those exact packages.
Before, only a push stamped the version, so a PR's packages could never be released as they were.
Now a PR build stamps the version the next release would get.
If a release happened in between, or main moved, the versions or files differ, and the push builds its own.
The PR changes the two workflows, four CI scripts, the digest agent and the merge rule, plus this page.
To undo it, revert the PR. A new commit on main always builds its own packages.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built from the jobs it folds and checked by a fresh review and this PR's own CI run. Thunar's code doesn't change.
The report job stays as it was for a fix; its report command also runs inside the review job.
The release steps reuse the same two scripts, unchanged.
And the summary script already ran from any job, so the summary workflow calls it the same way.
Both workflows and every script were checked for syntax in the building session.
The folded jobs and the billed minutes wait for this PR's first CI run.
A fresh review found seven issues; both serious ones are fixed, and three small ones are kept on purpose.
The first version ran the report beside the model, which could have left files or a process to steal the token.
And a fork's build cache could have slipped compiled code into a release, so forks are never reused.
The kept ones are small: wider write access on PR builds, a changelog wording, and a summary check not re-run.
The release from build, and reusing a merged PR's debs, first run when this PR merges.
The summary workflow's new path first runs on the next audit after the merge.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on this one; it closes the last of the minute-saving issues.
Together with pull request 69, CI now skips, caches, folds and reuses wherever it can.
lines.say: Together with pull request sixty-nine, CI now skips, caches, folds and reuses wherever it can.

lines.caption: After the merge, its own run should reuse this PR's debs, publish from build and skip verify.
The explainer job stays separate, since its check is part of the merge rule.
In short: the same checks, fewer billed minutes, and quieter PR comments.
